line: What about main circuits?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Well, you have to see it to believe it, sir. Those big crystals in there have come apart. Each of them unpeeling like the rind of an orange.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Analysis, Spock.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Our only hope now is rewiring impulse. But there are a thousand broken connections.

line: Mister Scott! More trouble with the circuit work.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: What now, Gabler?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: You sound like you're blathering, man. Wait, I'm coming.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Spock, are you slumping?

line: I have never slumped in my life, Captain, but I was about to ask you the same

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Security! Anyone, please! Mess Officer Briel requesting help in the Main Dining Room. Tables, chairs, silverware, everything seems to have enlarged. Women losing rings, hairpins. Some are near panic.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Captain, the most incredible thing is happening.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: We know. The whole ship has apparently expanded.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: An equally good possibility is that ship's personnel have contracted, and may be continuing to shrink.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Take us out of orbit, Mister Sulu. Shut down all unnecessary systems. Get every ounce of impulse power. We've got to get away from this planet.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Captain's log, stardate 5577.5. Our limited power attempt to escape the planet's gravity has failed. Undefined wave bombardment continues, resulting in a contraction of our bodies, or an expansion of the ship, by a factor of point three.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: No reply to our mayday, Captain. I don't believe we have enough power to transmit to Starbase Twenty Three.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Very well. Spock, what have you learned about the wave bombarding us?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Only that it is complex beyond anything in my experience.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Engineering to Captain Kirk.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Kirk here. How are they holding out, Scotty?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: We've replaced all the damaged parts we can. With all that's draining them, the well will soon enough run dry, sir.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Thank you, Scotty. Kirk out. Uhura, reduce mayday signals. One per ten minute cycle. Cut down sensor sweeps, Mister Arex.

title: The Terratin Incident

line: Then we can calculate the limits to our shrinkage.

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident
line: No information on that as yet, sir. I do have one read-out on full spiroid wave analysis. That will take approximately eight years.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Bypass that analysis. We've got twenty nine minutes before we're too small to operate ship controls. Everyone continue to jury-rig miniature control mechanisms. There's nothing more we can do.

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident

line: What good will it do to wait like this? Just one burst sir, one single

line: Sulu! I think his leg's broken. We'll need a splint.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Let's get him to Sickbay. Every one back to stations.

line: What happened?

line: In other words, we're going down to one sixteenth of an inch high.

line: Can you calculate the geographic center of the wave emissions from the planet's surface?

line: One, Scotty. Myself.

line: Captain's log, supplemental. There is one last measure we can take to try and stop the bombardment of the lethal spiroid wave. There must be some intelligence behind it. line: This is the best I could do in rigging so small a communicator, sir.

line: It's range cannot be guaranteed. How will we pinpoint you for return in case it fails?

line: Scotty, set automatic return for me. If there's anything to be found down there, ten minutes should do it.

title: The Terratin Incident

line: Captain, the transporter retains a memory of the body's molecular structure. Will it apply as well to your present height?

line: Kirk to Enterprise. I think we have an answer to the height problem. The transporter beam apparently returns our molecules to normal spacing. Kirk to Enterprise, do you read me?

line: I think I see

title: The Terratin Incident
line: I am Mendant of all this city, equal in command to yourself. We are people of pride, Captain, equal to your own. We neither suffer insult nor give apology for actions. But I give them now, for damage done your starship. Be assured, this land contains much dilithium to replace that you lost.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Where are my officers?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: I request you to understand. We tried to tell you our plight as you passed, that our adopted planet is dying. But our great antenna was buried. We had no choice but to use our invasion defense to reach you.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: You still haven't answered my question. Either you tell me what's happened to my people AREX [on viewscreen: Here we are, Captain.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: We're down here in the Capitol building of the Terratins, sir. They beamed us down with their transporters. See for yourself.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Spock, who are the Terratins? Where'd they come from?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Descendants of an early lost colony, which is why they retain some knowledge of starship methods such as transporter mechanisms. These Earth colonists named and numbered this planet Terra Ten.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Hence the present corruption of their name.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: There've been no Earth colonists a sixteenth of an inch tall.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Exactly why they were lost, Captain. Spirod epsilon waves are natural here, and shrank them to this size. It has become a genetic characteristic now.

line: Our ancestors were too small ever to be found again, Captain Kirk. We had to build our own world, master our own ways, our own defense. We sought no outsiders, asked no help. Now you see, Captain Kirk. We are about to lose all. We had to force help from your ship.

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident
line: They had no other way to reach us except to make us their size. They didn't mean us harm, sir.

line: I can help no one under present conditions. All Bridge crew prepare to beam aboard. Each of you carry as much dilithium as you can find.

line: The Captain orders dilithium. Bring the largest crystals in the city.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Bridge crew, prepare to beam up.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Energize, Captain.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Nice to be back aboard, sir, and fitting the room again.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: All crew personnel report to Transporter rooms immediately. Prepare to beam down to planet surface.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: The Terratins are making available all possible dilithium. The crystals are small, but I believe they will provide enough power until we can obtain larger pieces.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Sulu, take over the transporter here. Spock.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Inform your captain. Great earth cracks will soon swallow all. He must tell us. Shall we prepare to be rescued or to die?

title: The Terratin Incident
line: How's the helm, Sulu?

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Spock, the macroscope. Mendant, we welcome your people aboard the Enterprise.

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident
line: We're now headed for your new home. The planet Verdanis, ten days distant.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Is it beautiful, as we were told?

title: The Terratin Incident

title: The Terratin Incident
line: People of the Enterprise, we have no way to pay the debt we owe. But this at least comes from a meeting of all our numbers. We name you honorary Terratins now, and for all time to come.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: We came rather close to making it more than honorary.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Yes, I'd say just about a sixteenth of an inch close.

title: The Terratin Incident
line: Captain's log, supplemental. The Lilliputian city is to be taken to Verdanis and relocated on a fertile and well-watered plain. Then we'll be able to call the Terratin incident closed.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Captain's log, stardate 6063.4. The Enterprise is tracing the origin of a mysterious alien space probe. It approached the Federation home worlds, made a scan of Earth's system and then signaled outward into space. Before it could be intercepted, the probe self-destructed. We are following a trail of disrupted matter left by the probe's highly advanced propulsion system. Thus far, the trail has not intercepted any inhabited star systems.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Status report, Mister Spock.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: The trail is becoming fainter, Captain. I recommend we reduce speed to accommodate our sensors.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Reduce speed to warp factor two, Mister Walking Bear.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Aye, sir. Warp factor two.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Captain, sensors indicate a vessel at extreme range.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Course projection, Mister Arex.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It's coming in on the same course as the probe, sir. Heading toward us, warp three.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: No readings yet, Captain. Possibly a second probe.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Hmm. Or it could be the sender. Lieutenant Uhura, all stations to Yellow Alert. Standard hailing on all frequencies. Identification, Mister Spock?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: None as yet, sir. But sensors now indicate it is twice our size. Vessel appears extremely unorthodox in design. And Starfleet lists no other authorized vessels in this quadrant.

line: Reduce to warp one, Mister Walking Bear.

line: Maintain hailing.

line: Approaching ship has an immense energy field surrounding it. Fascinating. Readings indicate the vessel is composed entirely of crystalline ceramic. I would almost say

line: Captain, we're losing speed. The helm doesn't answer. We're going sublight.

line: Bridge to Engineering. Mister Scott, why are we losing speed?

line: Scott here, Captain. All our engines are still at full thrust, but it's just like we're ramming into a wall of clay. I don't know if the ship can take the strain.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I'm still checking, but it's minimal so far, sir. No structural damage or overheating. I think we were lucky.

line: McCoy here. No serious injuries. What the devil's going on?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Later, Bones.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We have been encased in a globular force field, Captain. The source is the approaching vessel.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But we hit at warp one. We should have been smashed.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It is a force globe, but one that is flexible enough to absorb any force. I cannot explain it. Clearly we cannot escape by simply fleeing. Sensors indicate we at now being probed.

line: Captain, there it is.

line: Other vessel is slowing.

line: Spock, status on other ship.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Still approaching, Captain. Going sublight. It continues to probe us. Its surrounding energy pattern is now shifting.

line: Have you ever seen anything like that, Spock?

line: Oh!

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I was angered because I believed you had forgotten me. But one in your midst knows my name. You will be given one chance to succeed where your ancestors failed. Fail me again and all of your kind shall perish.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Mister Walking Bear, how do you know who's aboard that ship?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I am a Comanche, Captain. I've studied the histories of many ancient Earth peoples, especially my own. That ship out there bears a strong resemblance to a god in Mayan and Aztec legends, Kukulkan.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Captain, library computer confirms that Ensign Walking Bear is correct. The Mayas had a legend of a winged serpent god who came from the skies, bringing knowledge. Such legends were not uncommon among Earth's peoples, Captain.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Then we could be dealing with the basis of all those legends. A space traveler who visited Earth in primitive times.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Entirely possible.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But why would Kukulkan want to destroy us?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You don't deserve it, Yeoman, but you're getting a few day's bed rest.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Mister Walking Bear, what do the legends say about

line: Walking Bear.

line: Captain, Security reports that Mister Scott and Doctor McCoy have also disappeared.

line: What's he doing to my crew?

line: Captain.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Captain's log, stardate 6063.5. First Officer Spock in temporary command. The Enterprise is the captive of an alien life form calling itself Kukulkan. Captain Kirk and three other officers have vanished. They most likely were transported by Kukulkan to his ship.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We must be somewhere inside that other ship.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: And us without a single phaser or communicator.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: At least I've got my medical kit, for all the good it is.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Mister Walking Bear, do the legends say what happened to Kukulkan?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: No, sir. Only that he left and promised one day to return.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Then that space probe that approached Earth must have been his. Listen.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We're being observed, watched.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Is there any way Spock could get through to us?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I don't think so, sir. Our sensors couldn't penetrate this ship.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Now I will show you the seeds that I have sown before. Learn from them. Find their purpose if you can. Only then will I appear before you.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I've never seen anything so beautiful.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Where did it come from?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Let's find out.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Mister Spock, shouldn't we be trying to find out what became of the Captain and the others?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Lieutenant Uhura, you are supposed to be monitoring the alien vessel. Our first priority is to free the Enterprise and ourselves. Return to your duties.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: They look like the obelisks built by the ancient Egyptians.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: With one difference, sir. Look at these carvings. That's not Egyptian. This gateway. I can't pin down what culture it represents.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But it's still a clue. This city is one gigantic riddle. Keep alert.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Now that we're here, what do we do?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Opinion, Mister Walking Bear.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Before he left, Kukulkan gave the Mayas a remarkably accurate calendar. He told them to build a city according to its cycles. On the date the city was finished, Kukulkan was supposed to return. The Mayas built their city and waited. Kukulkan never appeared.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Kukulkan must have visited several ancient peoples on Earth. But each one used only parts of his knowledge to build their cultures.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Does that mean they all tried to build something like this?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Yes, sir. But they all failed.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: If no one on Earth built this city exactly right, then that's why Kukulkan never came back. The entire city is our key.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Kukulkan said he would appear only when we learned its purpose.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Then there has to be some sort of signaling device here.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: That's odd. I've never seen a combination like this before.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: That pyramid seems to be the center of everything. I'm going up there. The rest of you spread out and circle it.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Look, sir. Another tower. And there's another tower down there. There must be one at all four corners.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: What's this?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Looks like there's a seam here. I think the head can be turned. Come on, lad. Give me a hand.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: The sun. That's it. Scotty, turn the head all the way around and aim it up here.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Aye, sir.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Turn the other heads this way! Bones, the serpent heads! Turn them to face the pyramid! I'm coming down.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: This is the last one, sir.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: The whole things is an energy amplification system. This is Kukulkan's signaling device.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: After scores of centuries, my design has been fulfillled. Behold me as I am.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Behold Kukulkan! Where are your weapons of destruction? Use them on me if you dare.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We have no weapons. And if we did, we would use them only with reason.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Where is your hate? You hate me, do you not? Why do you not speak to me of your hate?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But we don't hate you.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You fired your weapons at me.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We used them in self-defense. You fired on us.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I am your master. I may do with you as I will.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Do you think we belong to you?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Bones, Scotty, quiet.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It is as I thought. You have forgotten me and strayed from the path I set for you.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You say that we forgot you. How can you expect us to regard you as a deity if we don't remember you?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: If you do not know me, then it is my task to teach you.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Just once, I wish he'd let us use the stairs.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: What the devil is this place?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It looks like some kind of zoo. I don't recognize a lot of these species, Jim.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Please feel free to examine any of my specimens.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I could never be proud of putting wee beasties in cages.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But all of these lead a peaceful life, one that is safe and contented.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Contented? Cramped in these tiny cages?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: What you cannot see is that each of them, mentally, is in its own natural environment. They eat, breathe and live in worlds created by my machinery, worlds only they can see. They do not know they are in cages.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Then that city we were in wasn't really there.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Even so, I would hardly call your city our natural environment.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It was meant to be. That city and all else I taught to you ancestors. But they became evil.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But no one being, not even you, has the right to interfere with other cultures.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I have been alone all my life. Destruction fell on my race before your kind had diskovered fire. Creatures like these have been my only companions. I have seen you on many worlds. Savage, war-like, filled with self-hate, destroying yourselves in the end. At last I decided to help. As an experiment, I visited your Earth and tried to teach peaceful ways. I left, intending to return when I was summoned, but you never sent for me. Finally, I sent a probe. And what did I find? Warriors.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But we work only to create peace.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Nothing you have done so far makes me believe that is true. My creatures here have little intelligence. They alone live peacefully in the worlds I have to give. Even this creature, one of the fiercest and most untamable ever created, lives in peace in the world that I create for him.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Good heavens. This is a Capellan power-cat. No one's ever been able to keep one alive.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Why, Bones?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: They hate captivity. You try to put more than one hand on them and they throw off a charge of two thousand volts. How did you ever capture it?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It was an infant and easily controlled, as you were when I visited Earth. You still are children to me, to be led and shown how to live.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But if children are made totally dependent on their teachers, they will never be anything but children.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Enough! This is useless. Despite what I have shown you, you still cling to your disobedient ways. My dream is ending and all of you are to blame.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Of course. The elasticity of the force field can respond in only one direction at a time. All hands to battle stations. Full impulse power, helmsman. Tractor beam on, full power. Warp engines on standby. Mister Arex, prepare to compensate for warp catapult effect. When we break free, we will be thrown approximately five point six nine eight light years.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Compensation factors laid in, sir. But how are you going to break free?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: The force globe is flexible in only one direction per unit of time. We shall both push and pull on it simultaneously. It should become rigid enough for a burst of warp power to shatter it.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Force field contact in three seconds, sir.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Full warp power on my order. Now.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Reverse engines and come about. Lay in spiral evasive course for Kukulkan's ship.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Something is wrong. Escaped? But how? I will smash it this time.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Jim, the Enterprise broke free.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Then we've got to distract him and give Spock some time. Bones, what would happen if we pulled the cables on some of these cages.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Most of the animals would just lay there. Jim, the Capellan power-cat!

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Come on, Bones.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: No! Stop!

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Irrational savages. See what you have done.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Kukulkan, can't you control one of your own creatures?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I cannot. Your ship has disabled my central power source.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Jim, if that's true, we're all in trouble. Jim, do something.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Quick, your hypo. Full tranquilizer setting.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Did you inject that beast or yourself?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I'm fine, Bones. The cat's last power jolt clipped me.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It's just like a big kitten.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: What's this? My, aren't you the friendly little darling.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Kukulkan, I think we've earned the right to be heard.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You continue to take advantage of me, but I agree. Speak.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You think of us as being small creatures like this one. Are we really that inferior to you?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: No. But the violence of your kind surpasses even that of the power-cat.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: We'd be fools if we didn't know that. But we also have been using our minds and trying to learn to live in peace.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Because we have minds, we can't be what you wanted us to be. If we fail or succeed, it has to be our own doing. Intelligent life is too precious a thing to be led by the nose.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: But you are my children. I hoped I could teach you, help you.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: You did, long ago, when it was needed most. Our people were children then. Kukulkan, we've grown up now. We don't need you anymore.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I will let you go your own way. I have already done what I can.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Interesting, Captain. The creature was the Mayan god from the ancient legends.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: And the Toltec's Quetzalcoatl, the Chinese dragon and all the rest. But not quite a god. Just an old, lonely being who wanted to help others.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Spock, I wouldn't suppose that Vulcan has legends like those?

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Not legends, Doctor. Fact. Vulcan was visited by alien beings. They left much wiser.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: The other ship is getting underway, sir. Heading away from Earth.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: It's sad. Think what we could have done with his knowledge. But the price was just too high.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: I think I know how he felt, Jim. There's a line from Shakespeare.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Yes, Bones, I remember it. How sharper than a serpent's tooth it is to have a thankless child.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Indeed, Captain.

title: How Sharper Than A Serpent's Tooth
line: Lay in a course for Starbase Twenty One. All ahead, warp two.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain's log, stardate 6770.3. The Enterprise is on course for the planet Babel, where ambassadors from all Federation planets are waiting to honor the Enterprise's distinguished passenger, Commodore Robert April, first captain of the USS Enterprise, and for the past twenty years, Federation Ambassador at large. Now seventy five years old, Commodore April has reached mandatory retirement age.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: No matter where I've traveled in the galaxy, Jim, this bridge is more like home than anywhere else.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Commodore, I know the feeling.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: To me she was always like my child. I was there in the San Francisco Navy Yards when her unit components were built.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Jim, I didn't realize how many of the tools I use in Sickbay were designed by Sarah.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: As the first medical officer aboard a ship equipped with warp drive, I'm afraid I had to come up with new ideas all the time.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Your modesty is unnecessary, Mrs. April. Your achievements as a pioneer doctor in space are well known.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: And it's nice to know the lady is as intelligent as she is beautiful. Much like the flower she carries.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Oh, Doctor, flattery will get you everywhere. But I'm afraid my flower is dying.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It's a native of Capella Four, isn't it?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, but it has a life span of only a few hours. This morning it was a seedling, within a few hours it will be dead.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Excuse me, Captain. You asked to be notified when we made visual contact with the Beta Niobe nova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Thank you, Mister Spock. Mrs. April, you're about to see another of the galaxy's most beautiful sights, the Beta Niobe's supernova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It is beautiful, but also very deadly.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We're traveling at a safe distance from the nova, Mrs. April.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Beta Niobe. You were present when the star first started its explosion, Jim.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, we were, Commodore.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, sensors are picking up an unidentified object traveling at an incredible speed, presently on collision course with the Enterprise.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Put the ship on Red Alert. How fast is it traveling, Mister Spock?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: At a speed that should be impossible to achieve. Something on the order of warp thirty six.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: No natural object has ever been recorded as traveling at that speed.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I believe it is not a natural object, but a ship.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: But who would have the technology to build a ship that could travel at such a speed?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: No known race, Captain. Nevertheless, it will contact us in one point four minutes.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Hard about, helmsman. Change course for twenty four mark seven.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Correction, Captain. The ship was on a collision course only by coincidence. It is apparently heading for the heart of the Beta Niobe nova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: That's a course of self-destruction. Lieutenant Uhura, open hailing frequencies. I want to talk to that ship's captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, that ship is not responding.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: All right, if they won't talk, we'll slow them down. Mister Sulu, put a tractor beam on that ship.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Tractor beam on and operating, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We're having a small effect on other ship's speed, Captain. It has dropped to a speed of warp thirty two.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, they are making visual contact.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Put it on the screen, Lieutenant.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I've never heard that language before.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Nor I.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Run that message through the universal translator, Lieutenant Uhura. Perhaps it can tell us what language she is speaking in.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, the universal translator has the answer. The woman is speaking the same universal language we speak, but she is speaking in reverse.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Lieutenant, let's hear that tape backward, which should sound forward to us.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, sir, on the screen.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I am on a priority mission. Your beam is slowing my progress. Release my ship at once or I am doomed.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Open hailing frequencies again, Lieutenant. Tell her she is endangering her life if she remains on her present course.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: No use, sir. She's refusing to answer.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Scotty, what is it?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, the engines are buckling. We cannot keep up at this speed.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Mister Arex, what is our speed?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Now at warp eleven, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Mister Spock, how long until the alien vessel makes contact with the Beta Niobe nova?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Three minutes forty two point seven seconds.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Give me three and a half minutes, Scotty.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Still increasing speed, Captain. Warp fourteen. Warp fifteen.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I have no choice. I have to release the tractor beam. I can't destroy this ship and four hundred and thirty people to save one person. Mister Sulu, release our beam.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Sir, I can't release the tractor beam.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: What do you mean, Mister Sulu?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Our controls are inoperative. The ship isn't responding like it should.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Go to manual override.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: NO responding, sir.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We've got to release that beam, or we're going to follow that ship into the nova!

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Our speed is now warp twenty, and the other ship will contact the nova in one minute fifty eight point three seconds.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I'm sorry, Commodore, Mrs. April. It looks as though we may not reach Babel.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: As starship personnel, we were always prepared to give our lives, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We are still starship personnel, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: There's still one chance. After that ship enters the nova, it should burn up and break contact with our tractor beam. Mister Spock, how long will we have to apply full braking power and execute course change?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We are up to warp twenty two and increasing, Captain. We shall have forty two point eight five seconds to correct our course after the alien ship enters the nova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: You heard that, Mister Sulu.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Aye, aye, sir.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Mister Scott, we're going to apply full braking power in a minute.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Aye, Captain. Our engines are almost gone.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: They've only lasted this long at this speed because the alien vessel is pulling us with our own tractor beam.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: The alien vessel will contact Beta Niobe in fifty two point three seconds, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Contact in thirty nine seconds. Thirty eight, thirty seven

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Thirteen, twelve, eleven

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Get ready to execute course change, Mister Sulu.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, sir.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Now, Mister Sulu!

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Something's wrong, Captain. We're still being pulled by the alien ship.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Impossible. It should have been destroyed instantly.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Apparently it was not, Captain. Our tractor beam is still connected to her.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: And we are still increasing speed. Contact with the nova in thirty five point one eight seconds.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: That other ship may have been able to survive the heat of a nova, but the Enterprise can't. Mister Scott, how about that full braking power?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We're as badly off as before, Captain. We have no control of the ship as long as that alien lassie has us in tow.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Contact in twenty seconds.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Keep trying those controls, Mister Sulu.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Still no change, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It's got to work.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Fourteen seconds, thirteen, twelve

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Never mind, Mister Spock, it's no use.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We're still here. Lieutenant Uhura, can you get us a visual?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: What?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Where are we?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain's log, stardate 6770.6. The Enterprise has passed into the most alien landscape I have ever seen. We are in some reverse universe where black stars shine in a white void. We are still in the tow of the alien ship, both of us having survived the extreme heat of the Beta Niobe nova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: This is Scott calling the Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Scotty. How are we doing down there?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Well, we just had to learn to run the ship all over again. Every control is working in reverse.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: All right. Lieutenant Uhura, we're going to contact that ship again. We need some answers.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain Kirk. The Capellan flower!

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I'm sure Captain Kirk has other problems besides your flower, dear.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: You don't understand. Before we entered this universe it was about to die. and now it's in full bloom again.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: How's that possible?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It's as if it were growing younger again. I can almost feel it while I'm holding it.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, the flower is not the only thing on board that is growing younger.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Explain, Spock.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Ship's chronometers are also running backward. The flow of time is reversed in this universe. The longer we stay here, the younger we will become.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: The alien ship is responding to our call, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Your interference almost cost me my life.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I can understand her now, without the aid of the universal translator.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Apparently our brains are also working in reverse, Captain, so we can now understand her language. That is why the ship seems to be operating in the reverse to us.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I'm Captain James T Kirk of the USS Enterprise. We tried to prevent you from entering the Beta Niobe nova. We assumed your ship would burn up.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I had to return to my own universe, Captain Kirk.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Who are you? How did you come to be in our universe?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I am an explorer of space. I was caught unaware when Amphion, previously a dead star, went nova and came to life. I was pulled into the star. But instead of burning up, I passed into a universe where everything operates in reverse to my universe.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Our universe.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes. My theory is that two stars going nova in the same place in both universes created a gateway which I passed through.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: In her universe, a nova is a dead star which comes to life! And when the explosions of a nova in her universe and one in our universe occur together, it's possible to travel between the two universes.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Then we must return the same way, through the two novas.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: That would be impossible, Captain. Amphion is no longer nova. It has begun it's life as a star. I suggest you set a course to follow my ship. Perhaps our scientists can help solve your problem.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We have little choice.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain's log, supplemental. We are proceeding to Karla Five's planet, Arret.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Gentlemen, I'm sure none of us mind growing younger instead of older for a change.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It pleases me, Jim. If we stay here long enough, I'll no longer be at the mandatory retirement age.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Nevertheless, we must return home and I am open to suggestions.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It is logical that we must reproduce the conditions that brought us here. Two novas must occupy the same space in both universes in order to create a gateway for us to travel through. One star dying in our universe, and one being born here would recreate the correct conditions.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: That would take a remarkable coincidence, Mister Spock.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, we are approaching Arret. Karla Five is asking if you are prepared to beam down to the planet.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Tell Karla Five that Mister Spock, Commodore April and myself will be beaming down. UHURA [on monitor}: Yes, sir.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Karla Five has given us coordinates to beam down to her son's laboratory, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Her son? We don't have time for children's games right now, Scotty, but beam us down.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Aye, sir.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: May I introduce my son, Karl Four.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: My honor to meet you, gentlemen.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Most logical. If the flow of time is reversed, then one is born at an old age, and dies in infancy. Your descendants are born before you, and your ancestors are born after you.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Then the young child in the playpen

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: My father, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We could remain forever awed with the differences between our universes, Karla Five, but we must diskover a way to return to our positive matter universe.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Exactly the problem I have been working on since Karla informed me of your troubles, Captain Kirk. This is a map of our galaxy. Our home solar system is here. You entered our universe through the Amphion nova, here.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We need to coordinate this to our own universe. Can we do that, Spock?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Captain. Apparently the two universes occupy the same space, but in different dimensions.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Assuming Beta Niobe and Amphion occupy the same space, we can determine if there are any other novas occupying the same space in both universes.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Correct, Commodore. Now if you'll watch the star map, you'll see the Milky Way. Here is Beta Niobe, and here is Earth. It corresponds exactly with Arret. By superimposing both star maps, we will see where two stars occupy the same place in both universes. The red spheres indicate where two stars are in the same space. No pair are novas in both universes.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: If stars begin as dead stars here then we could bring one of them to life prematurely.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, we could act as a midwife giving birth to a star. Then we would have two novas in the same position and theoretically return home.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: But I had to pass through the novas at my ship's top speed to avoid burning up. Your ship isn't capable of such a speed.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: That's true, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: You are welcome to use my ship, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I have a crew of four hundred and thirty, Karla Five. Your ship is suitable for only a few people.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We can't use her ship to transport us, Captain, but we could use it as an unmanned ship with our tractor beam attached.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It could work. That's how we arrived here in the first place.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It should work, yes. But any miscalculation anywhere along the way and we'll be plunging tail first into a supernova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain's log, stardate 6770.1. Time continues to flow backward for us. We have set course for a dead star in this anti-matter universe that corresponds with the nova Minara in ours. We're being pulled by Karla Five's unmanned vessel, which is equipped with enough positive matter armament to ignite the dead star into life.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: we just might get you to Babel after all, Commodore.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I'll be glad to get home, but not necessarily to Babel. It only means the end of my career, Jim.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Message coming in from Arret, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I want to wish you luck, Captain. Whether you succeed or fail, the outcome will remain unknown to me.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Karla Five. We'll burn to a crisp or escape into our own universe. Either way, you'll never hear from us again. Thank you for the sacrifice of your vessel.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: It is a small sacrifice, Captain Kirk. Success.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Tractor beam working properly, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We're meeting the speed of Karla Five's unmanned vessel, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: How much time before the youngest crew member returns to the time of birth?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Eighteen minutes thirty seven seconds in real time. But long before that we shall all be children. And, Captain, that also means we are losing our knowledge at an alarming rate. It is possible we will soon be unable to operate the Enterprise.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: How is our course, Mister Sulu?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I don't know. What am I doing here? What is all this equipment?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: He's too young, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Mister Arex, take over for him. Lieutenant Uhura, report to navigation console.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I'm sorry, sir, I don't understand all this equipment. What do I do with these controls?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Never mind. Spock, can you fill in for Sulu and Uhura?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Captain, but who will fill in for you?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: What do you mean?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: At what age did you become a starship captain? And when did you enter Starfleet Academy?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: I see what you mean.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: As a Vulcan, I age the slowest. I will be capable of assuming command longer than anyone else. But even I will become too young to know what to do.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain's log, supplemental. We have eleven minutes of real time left to reach the dead star, but all around my crew are turning into children, unable to operate the ship.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Ten minutes fourteen point twenty one seconds, Captain. We shall arrive with only moments to spare. We will need to diskonnect the tractor beam at the appropriate time.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Tractor beam? How do we do that, Spock?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Captain, I must assume command. You are no longer able to command the Enterprise.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Whatever you say. What shall I do?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Mister Spock, as long as I am aboard, I am senior officer. I hate to pull rank, but you will be capable of command only for a few minutes, not long enough to complete the maneuvers necessary to take us home.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: You are correct, of course. Commodore April, command is yours.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Commodore? I'm Captain April, Mister Spock.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Robert, we're the only adults on the bridge. They're all teenagers and children.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Make sure no harm comes to them, Sarah. We have to ignite that dead star if we're going home. Mister Spock, you are still capable of following orders?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Yes, Captain.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Very good. Assume your post at the navigation console.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: The dead star is directly ahead, Captain, twelve degrees south of galactic plane.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Arm Karla Five's vessel, Spock.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Vessel armed, Captain. Nine seconds to impact. Eight, seven,

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Three, two

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Hang on, we're going right into the heart of the nova.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We did it! We're home again! We're all right. We're home. The reverse aging process has stopped.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: But the Enterprise crew, they're all children.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: They can enter the transporter. It retains a memory of their original molecular structure.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: But what about us? We don't have to use the transporter. We can remain young, live our lives over again. You could command a starship once more.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: What a blessing to be able to live one's life over again, if the life you've led has left you unfulfillled. No Sarah, I don't want to live it all over again. I couldn't improve one bit on what we've had together.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Oh, Robert.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: We've received a message from the Federation that might bring you some cheer. Lieutenant Uhura, would you relay it to Commodore April and his wife?

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: In view of Commodore April's heroic actions aboard the USS Enterprise this stardate, we are reviewing his mandatory retirement, and will consider his appeal to remain Federation Ambassador at large.

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Well, good. Just because someone is seventy five years old doesn't mean they're ready to stop giving service to the galaxy!

title: The Counter-Clock Incident
line: Arriving at Babel in one hour fifteen minutes, Captain.
